info.description:
The SuperSend API enables programmatic access to manage contacts, campaigns, teams, senders, and events.

## Base URL

All API requests should be made to:
```
https://api.supersend.io/v2
```

## Authentication

Authenticate requests using your API key in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

## Rate Limits

- Standard: 100 requests/minute
- Bulk operations: 10 requests/minute
- List operations: 60 requests/minute

## Errors

All errors follow a consistent format with `type`, `code`, `message`, and `request_id`.
info.title: SuperSend API

delete.description:
Archives a campaign (soft delete) and its contacts. The campaign is paused and hidden from default lists.
Draft campaigns are permanently removed.

Teams must retain at least one non-archived campaign; deleting the last eligible campaign returns **409**.

Updates campaign fields. Only provided fields are updated.
Some fields cannot be modified on active campaigns.

get.description:
Everything to check before launching a campaign, in one call: the steps on the main path
(subjects, waits, LinkedIn actions), who sends (sender profiles, inboxes, warmup), who receives
(contacts by state), the schedule and daily volume, and the launch checks.

`checks` combines the dashboard's start checklist with the trial/plan gate (all `blocking: true`),
plus warnings that don't block launch (`blocking: false`), such as no contacts waiting or inboxes
still warming. `can_launch` is true when the campaign is not already active and no blocking check
fails.

Sequences longer than 12 steps list the first 12 in `sequence.steps`; `sequence.total_steps` has
the full count. Waits are folded into `wait_before` on the step that follows them.

Returns **404** for campaigns that don't exist or belong to another organization, and **403**
when the campaign is in your organization but you are not on its team.

At least one active email sender
At least one sender profile with LinkedIn identity

get.description:
Retrieves the sequence (nodes and edges) for a campaign.
This endpoint provides detailed access to the visual sequence builder structure.

The sequence defines the automation flow including:
- Start and stop nodes
- Email, LinkedIn action nodes
- Wait/delay nodes
- Conditional logic (If/Switch nodes)
- HTTP API request nodes
- Task and note nodes

patch.description:
Updates the sequence (nodes and/or edges) for a campaign.

**Important notes:**
- Providing `nodes` replaces ALL existing nodes
- Providing `edges` replaces ALL existing edges
- Omitting a field leaves it unchanged

**Validation rules:**
- If/Switch nodes cannot exceed 10 paths/cases
- Each path cannot exceed 10 conditions
- All node and edge IDs should be valid UUIDs

post.description:
Creates a new contact or updates an existing one (upsert by email/LinkedIn), or
creates/updates **team contact profile only** when `CampaignId` is omitted or null (no campaign
enrollment row).

**Campaign enrollment:** When `CampaignId` is set, returns the created/updated **contact**
(enrollment). Optional `contact_profile_id` seeds the enrollment from an existing profile;
the profile must already have a **ContactTeam** row for the campaign's team.

**Profile-only (no campaign):** Omit `CampaignId` (or send null/empty). Requires `TeamId` and
at least one of `email` or `linkedin_url`. Returns `201` with `data.object`:
`contact_profile` and `enrolled: false` (no `Contact` row).

**Flow:** With `CampaignId`, the API upserts **ContactProfile** + **ContactTeam** for the team,
then creates or updates the **Contact** (campaign enrollment). Without `CampaignId`, only the
profile and team membership are upserted.

**Repeats and retries:** An existing enrollment is matched by `CampaignId` plus `email` (or
`linkedin_url` when there is no email), case-insensitive. Sending the same contact to the same
campaign again — including concurrent or retried requests — updates that enrollment (`200`)
instead of enrolling the person twice, and keeps its A/B variant. If another request for the
same contact and campaign is still being processed after about 10 seconds, the API returns
`409` `contact_enrollment_in_progress`; retry after a few seconds. `integration_contact_id` is
stored but not used for matching.

**Email validation:** Set `validate_emails: true` to queue deliverability verification when the
contact profile is **unvalidated or pending** (`valid2` -1 or 0). Already-validated profiles
are not re-checked (no extra credits). Applies on create, update, and re-enroll. Default is
false. Not applied on the profile-only path.

error.message: Another request is adding this contact to this campaign. Retry in a few seconds.

409.description: Another request for the same contact and campaign is still being processed; retry after a few seconds

post.description:
Import contacts in bulk via JSON array or CSV file upload.
Processing happens asynchronously - returns an upload ID for tracking.

**JSON Body:**
```json
{
  "contacts": [
    { "email": "john@example.com", "first_name": "John" },
    { "email": "jane@example.com", "first_name": "Jane" }
  ],
  "TeamId": "uuid",
  "CampaignId": "uuid"
}
```

**CSV Upload:**
Use `multipart/form-data` with:
- `contacts`: CSV file
- `TeamId`: Team UUID
- `CampaignId`: Campaign UUID
- `mapping_fields`: JSON mapping of CSV columns to contact fields
- `validate_emails`: Optional. Set to `true` to run email verification (consumes credits). Default `false`.

**Email Validation:**
Set `validate_emails: true` to queue verification for contacts in the import (consumes credits).
Default is false to avoid surprise billing. Applies to both JSON and CSV uploads. For single-contact
upsert (`POST /contacts`), already-validated profiles are not re-checked.

**Limits:**
- Maximum 50,000 contacts per request
- No limit on total contacts (contacts are unlimited on every plan)

owner's nameserver change, looks the nameservers up live first. Returns the nameservers to set
(`nameservers.set_to`), whether they're live (`nameservers.verified`), the domain's inboxes,
and `next`.

`stage` is one of: `connected` (nothing to do until inboxes are bought), `preparing_nameservers`
(inboxes paid; nameservers ready in a few minutes), `awaiting_nameservers` (set the nameservers
shown at the registrar), `ready` (inboxes being created or live), `setting_up` (bought through
SuperSend, still registering), `unavailable` (cancelled, expired or failed).

data.name: tryacme.com
data.next: This domain is registered outside SuperSend. At the registrar where tryacme.com is registered, replace all of its nameservers with: ada.ns.example.net, bob.ns.example.net. ...

post.description:

The response includes email intelligence fields (risk score, flags, provider hints, network metrics) in the
same payload as the SMTP result—one verification credit unlocks both.

get.description:
Returns deliverability diagnosis for a team: reply rate, bounce breakdown,
placement test results, target mix (Gmail/Outlook/corporate), and recommendations.
Use for questions like "Why is my reply rate low?"

**Bounce data:** `bounce_categories` and `bounce_types` are both derived from **send/bounce
events** (`Events.bounce_category` and `Events.bounce_subtype`). Each `bounce_types[]` row
includes `category` from the event; `percentage` is the share of that subtype within its
**category bucket** (so lines under a category sum to ~100% when subtypes are fully populated).

get.description:
One call to see what an account still needs before it can send: billing (trial or plan),
inboxes and warmup, sender profiles, LinkedIn accounts, and campaigns.

`next_steps` lists what is missing, in order. Each step says who does it: `agent` (with the
MCP tool and API call to use), `human` (with a dashboard link for browser-only steps such as
adding a card or Google/Microsoft sign-in), or `human_or_agent`.

Warmup counts as done 14 days after it starts. `ready_to_send` is true when billing allows
sending and at least one sender profile has an active inbox.

parameters.description: Team to check. Defaults to the caller's default team, then their oldest team.
parameters.name: team_id

next_steps.why: Campaigns send from sender profiles. Put the inboxes in a sender profile, then assign it to campaigns.
No campaigns yet. Build the sequence, assign a sender profile, and import contacts.

post.description:
Plans sending domains and inboxes without spending money, then returns a prefilled checkout
link for a human to review and pay. **Nothing is charged by this call.**

Domains can be new (checked that they can be bought) or ones the organization already has:
bought through SuperSend, or connected with `POST /domains/connect`. Owned domains come back
with `owned: true` and `price_per_year: 0`; only their inboxes are charged. Inbox limits count
the inboxes already on a domain (5 per domain, one provider per domain).

After payment, DNS is set up automatically and new inboxes appear within 24-48 hours and start
warming. The exception is a connected domain registered outside SuperSend
(`nameserver_change_required: true`): a few minutes after payment,
`POST /domains/{id}/verify` returns the two nameservers to set at its registrar, and its
inboxes are created once they're live. Track progress with `GET /setup`.

data.next: Give the user this link. They review the cart, add domain contact details, and pay. DNS is set up automatically, and new inboxes appear within 24-48 hours and start warming. Check progress with get_setup_status (GET /v2/setup).

200.description: Checkout link and cost estimate (nothing charged)

error.message: These domains can't be bought: acme.com (taken). Pick other names and try again.

422.description: One or more domains can't be bought. `error.details.unavailable` lists each domain and why.
